title: Rate-One Quantum-Secure Tweakable Block Ciphers
summary: Classical LRW achieves rate one from a PRP assumption, but a quantum-secure rate-one tweakable block cipher using only a qPRP assumption remains open without related-key security.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether a rate-one quantum-secure tweakable block cipher can be constructed from a block cipher under a quantum-secure pseudorandom-permutation assumption alone, without assuming related-key security. Here, rate one means one block-cipher call per tweakable-block-cipher call; the classical LRW approach achieves this rate from a pseudorandom-permutation assumption, whereas the quantum-secure key-tweak-insertion construction requires related-key security and the LRW approach does not appear applicable without it. [S1]

scope.domain: Construction of quantum-secure tweakable block ciphers from block ciphers.
assumptions: The underlying block cipher satisfies a quantum-secure pseudorandom-permutation assumption.
parameters: Rate one: one block-cipher call per tweakable-block-cipher call
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a rate-one quantum-secure tweakable block cipher can be built under only the qPRP assumption, without related-key security.

progress.summary: The source contrasts classical LRW, which attains rate one from a PRP assumption, with the quantum-secure key-tweak-insertion construction, which requires related-key security. It leaves the qPRP-only case open and notes that LRW does not seem applicable.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., QCB: Efficient Quantum-secure Authenticated Encryption
